# Our predicted Socceroos' World Cup XI
[...]
Tony Popovic is taking 26 men to Vancouver, Seattle, Santa Clara and then hopefully elsewhere around the three host nations. Here's who we expect to be starting the opening match against Turkey on June 14 (AEST).
[...]
Predicted Australia XIFlashscore
[...]
## Starting goalkeeper: Maty Ryan
[...]
## Left wing back: Jordy Bos
[...]
Feyenoord(Eredivisie)
[...]
## Centre back: Lucas Herrington
[...]
## Centre back: Harry Souttar
[...]
## Centre back: Alessandro Circati
[...]
## Right wing back: Jacob Italiano
[...]
## Central midfield: Aiden O'Neill
[...]
## Central midfield: Jackson Irvine
[...]
## Left wing: Connor Metcalfe
[...]
The starting lineup in the opening warm-up game against Mexico at the Rose Bowl dropped a big hint about Popovic's ideal midfield and observant readers would have noticed the St Pauli logo twice in the starting XI.
[...]
## Central striker: Mohamed Touré
[...]
## Right wing: Mathew Leckie
[...]
This has to be by far the most difficult position to predict as there does not appear to be any clear incumbent nor any major standout, not to mention the late addition of Cristian Volpato into the final squad throwing a cat amongst the pigeons as far as selection goes
[...]
That's where 35-year-old Leckie comes in. Leckie made a recent return from injury but played a whole 120 minutes in an A-League semi-final loss to Auckland FC, started in right midfield against Mexico, and is a trusted veteran who Popovic is intimately familiar with.
[...]
We're expecting Volpato to grow into the tournament and perhaps even impress off the bench, but with Metcalfe also a right midfield option, experience is likely to prevail for the first game in cool Vancouver conditions.
[...]
## Australia will face Turkey in Vancouver at 2pm AEST this Sunday.

Deschamps has also omitted Eduardo Camavinga from his selection, but Real Madrid teammate Aurelien Tchouameni has been called up to a five-strong midfield selection, also comprising Adrien Rabiot, Warren Zaire-Emery, Manu Kone and the veteran N'Golo Kante.

## France World Cup 2026 predicted XI
[...]
With such a star-studded selection of players to choose from, Deschamps will have to make extremely difficult decisions in all areas of the field, but perpetual headline-grabber Kylian Mbappe can at least be assured of his place in the XI - so long as he is fit.
[...]
Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembele and Bayern Munich hotshot Michael Olise are attacking shoo-ins too, forcing Desire Doue, Rayan Cherki, Bradley Barcola and Marcus Thuram to fight for the final attacking spot.
[...]
Regardless of any off-field chaos at Real Madrid, Aurelien Tchouameni is a sure-fire pick in the heart of midfield, potentially alongside long-time Deschamps favourite Adrien Rabiot thanks to his stellar form for AC Milan this season.
[...]
Jules Kounde and Theo Hernandez are the standout right and left-back options respectively, but a fascinating three-way fight for central defensive starts will emerge between Dayot Upamecano, Ibrahima Konate and William Saliba.

# How we think the Socceroos will line up against Turkiye in World Cup opener, with two spots debatable
[...]
With the squad locked in and the days ticking down, the Socceroos’ first match at the World Cup is within sight.
[...]
Tony Popovic and his team played two warm-up matches in the United States, going down 1-0 to Mexico in Pasadena and drawing 1-1 with Switzerland in San Diego. Now all eyes are on the opening clash against Turkiye in Vancouver.
[...]
These two matches have given a glimpse as to how Australia could line up in that clash, with really only two major question marks still remaining in the XI.
[...]
Football360 predicts how we think Australia will line up against Turkiye on June 14 AEST.
[...]
Goalkeeper: Maty Ryan
[...]
Maty Ryan is the captain of the Socceroos and will become one of just four players to represent Austraia at four World Cups alongside Tim Cahill, Mark Milligan and current teammate Mathew Leckie.
[...]
He’s coming off a stellar season with Levane in LaLiga and will start the opening match.
[...]
Centre-back: Harry Souttar
[...]
22, Harry Souttar has come off a lengthy injury layoff to be fit again for the World Cup – and he will start.
[...]
Centre-back: Alessandro Circati
[...]
Still just 22 years old, he has become the bedrock of this rearguard and will be a walk-up starter in the starting XI for this tournament, if fit.
[...]
Centre-back: Lucas Herrington
[...]

Right wing-back: Jacob Italiano
[...]
Jacob Italiano impressed from the outset when he first joined the Socceroos setup last year and, barring unforeseen circumstances, he will start at right wing-back throughout this World Cup.
